name: CSA W47.1 / W59 (Fusion Welding of Steel — Company Certification)
description: CSA W47.1 certifies a company — not an individual — to perform fusion welding of steel, administered by the Canadian Welding Bureau. Certification is granted in a division (1, 2.1, 2.2 or 3) that limits what the company may weld and how much engineering oversight it requires, and it depends on holding a qualified welding engineer or supervisor, qualified procedures, qualified welders with current continuity, and passing periodic CWB audit. CSA W59:24 provides the workmanship and design requirements the welding must satisfy. W47.1:25 was published in May 2025, so a certificate issued against the seventh edition warrants a currency check.
scope: Companies performing fusion welding of steel, including fabrication shops and field welding

families.name: Company Certification and Oversight
families.description: The certificate, its division limits, and the qualified people it depends on.

controls.name: Current Certification and Division Scope
controls.description: A current W47.1 certificate is held, and work accepted stays within the certified division and material scope; the certificate edition and expiry are tracked.

controls.name: Qualified Welding Procedure Specifications
controls.description: Welding procedure specifications are qualified and CWB-accepted for the joints, materials, positions and processes used, are current, and are available at the point of work.

controls.name: Welding Engineer or Supervisor of Record
controls.description: A qualified welding engineer or supervisor as required by the certified division is on record, currently qualified, with a succession arrangement so the certificate is not exposed to one departure.

controls.name: CWB Audit and Corrective Action
controls.description: Periodic CWB audits are passed, findings are corrected within the required period, and audit correspondence is retained.

families.name: Welder Qualification and Continuity
families.description: The individual-level records a CWB auditor and a client inspector both sample.

controls.name: Welder Qualification to Procedure
controls.description: Welders are qualified for the procedures, positions and processes they perform, with qualification test records retained and identification traceable to their welds.

controls.name: Continuity of Qualification
controls.description: Welder qualification continuity is tracked against the required interval, and a welder whose continuity has lapsed is requalified before performing certified work.

families.name: Workmanship and Inspection (CSA W59)
families.description: Executing and verifying the weld to the workmanship standard.

controls.name: Consumable Control and Storage
controls.description: Welding consumables are the specified classification, controlled by lot, and stored and conditioned per manufacturer requirement.

controls.name: Visual Inspection and Acceptance Criteria
controls.description: Welds are visually inspected against W59 acceptance criteria by qualified inspection personnel, with results recorded.

controls.name: Non-Destructive Examination
controls.description: Where NDE is specified, it is performed by certified personnel to a written procedure and results are recorded and retained.

controls.name: Weld Repair and Nonconformance
controls.description: Rejected welds are repaired to a qualified repair procedure and re-inspected, with the nonconformance and disposition recorded.
